subject: gk
question: The revenue raised by the central bank through printing of money is called ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Seigniorage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Seigniorage** is the profit made by a central bank from issuing currency, especially the difference between the face value of coins or notes and their production costs.
 
• This economic term originates from the Old French word "seigneuriage," which referred to the right of the lord to coin money.
 
• Seigniorage serves as a source of revenue for governments, helping to finance various public expenditures without raising taxes.
 
• The concept is crucial in understanding how central banks manage monetary policy and control inflation.
 
• Seigniorage can also refer to the benefits reaped from the inflation tax, where the real value of currency held by the public decreases as inflation rises.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inflation Tax**

 
 
• The inflation tax refers to the loss of purchasing power experienced by holders of cash and cash equivalents due to inflation.
 
• It acts as an implicit tax on holders of money, as the real value of their holdings decreases over time.
 
• Governments benefit from this as it reduces the real value of their debt.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy**
 
 
• Monetary policy involves the management of interest rates and the total supply of money in circulation, typically carried out by central banks.
 
• It aims to control inflation, manage employment levels, and ensure economic stability.
 
 
 
• **Fiat Currency**
 
 
• Fiat currency is government-issued currency that is not backed by a physical commodity like gold or silver.
 
• The value of fiat money is derived from the relationship between supply and demand and the stability of the issuing government.
 
 
 
• **Quantitative Easing**
 
 
• Quantitative easing (QE) is a monetary policy where a central bank buys government securities or other securities from the market to increase the money supply and encourage lending and investment.
 
• It is used to stimulate the economy when standard monetary policy has become ineffective.
